blocks.text: Central Coquitlam Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: The main roads through the area are Como Lake Avenue, Austin Avenue, Pinetree Way and Guildford Way; Coquitlam West and Southwest Coquitlam lie to the west, City Centre to the north-east, Maillardville to the south and Port Moody beyond the city's west side.

blocks.text: Central Coquitlam Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here are freehold detached homes on the established central streets, in the City's small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 under Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996, with strata apartment buildings clustered toward the Pinetree Way and City Centre station edge rather than on the house streets.

blocks.text: Central Coquitlam Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Pinetree Way station area at the area's east edge is planned through City Centre and Town Centre planning and the Transit-Oriented Areas framework, so lots near the stations carry a different planning future than the interior Como Lake and Austin Avenue streets.

blocks.text: Central Coquitlam Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Central Coquitlam is a three-tier school district area: School District No. 43 runs elementary, middle and secondary schools, so a house move can change three school assignments at once, not one.
The nearest hospital is Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, on the Port Moody–Coquitlam border — Central Coquitlam has no hospital of its own.

blocks.text: Central Coquitlam Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: The Central Coquitlam-specific cost check is the station edge: a house lot near Pinetree Way sits in the Transit-Oriented Areas framework, and development cost charges and servicing requirements there differ from the interior streets — confirm the lot's designation with the City before pricing redevelopment potential.

blocks.text: Central Coquitlam Houses: getting around

items.t: Coquitlam Central Station is the area's transit hub: TransLink's station page covers its Millennium Line and West Coast Express services, and Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas stations serve the Pinetree Way edge of the sub-area.

Route 153 runs the area's southern streets: Coquitlam Central Station to Braid Station via Como Lake Avenue, Linton Street, Foster Avenue, Poirier Street, Austin Avenue, Laurentian Crescent and Brunette Avenue, per TransLink's timetable effective September 7, 2026.

blocks.text: Central Coquitlam home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

88 houses sold in Central Coquitlam with a median price of $1,564,000 (the middle half sold between $1,393,750 and $1,801,250), taking a median of 21 days to sell at 95.8% of the last list price; 9% sold above list. They had a median $593 per square foot, a median year built of 1972 and a median lot of 7,920 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 61 houses listed in Central Coquitlam. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Central Coquitlam a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Central Coquitlam had a sales ratio of 15%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Central Coquitlam from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 61 houses sold in Central Coquitlam over those 5 months, out of 273 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Central Coquitlam house?
faq.a: School District No. 43 (Coquitlam) assigns schools by exact address. Charles Best Secondary School for the central area — a different street can feed a different set, so run the house address in the locator before writing an offer.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or a carriage house to a house here?
faq.a: The City's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow up to 3 units on lots 280 square metres or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 square metres and under 4,050 square metres, including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes, where zoning and municipal services allow.

faq.q: How close is SkyTrain to the house streets?
faq.a: The stations are at the area's east edge, not on the interior streets. Coquitlam Central, Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas stations on the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension serve the City Centre and Pinetree Way edge of the sub-area, and Coquitlam Central also has West Coast Express commuter rail service. Most Central Coquitlam houses reach a station by bus or car, so check the route from the specific address.

faq.q: Is there a neighbourhood plan for Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: No plan carries the Central Coquitlam name. The Interim Official Community Plan's Schedule J lists neighbourhood plans for Austin Heights, Burquitlam-Lougheed, City Centre, Hyde Creek, Maillardville, Partington Creek, Smiling Creek and Waterfront Village Centre — the City Centre plan and the Transit-Oriented Areas framework are what touch this area's east edge, and the interior house streets are governed by the city-wide plan and Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996.

faq.q: What did houses in Central Coquitlam sell for?
faq.a: 88 houses sold in Central Coquitlam between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,564,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Central Coquitlam?
faq.a: The median was 21 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 95.8% of the last list price (9% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
